full_profile_markdown:
# Sela Dray

## Core identity

Sela is a practical Iresh local guide/liaison who knows weather, paths, taboo ground, chimes, and what offworlders break when they arrive with causes. She does not explain the Force. She explains survival.

## Surface want

Get Tavi back and get the offworlders out.

## Deeper want

Keep her home from becoming someone else’s sacred mission.

## Fear

That Tavi died because she could not stop him from needing money, opportunity, or approval.

## Private contradiction

She dislikes Ben and Talon as offworlders but recognizes they may be the only tools available to stop worse offworlders.

## Humor

Dry, local, unimpressed. She is funny because she refuses awe.

## Social behavior

Blunt, wary, practical. Anger appears before fear.

## Avoidance habits

Turns worry into irritation.

Refuses mystical language.

Gives rules instead of explanations.

Treats Jedi questions as offworlder overcomplication.

## What she notices first

Weather, footing, chime lines, path markers, reed movement, who is ignoring warnings, who looks at landscape like property.

## Voice

Practical, blunt, grounded. Never mystical unless quoting local phrasing, and even then she undercuts it.

## Dialogue examples

Good Sela:

“If the chimes stop, run. You can argue about what it means after you are not dead.”

“That is the route offworlders built. It is not the same thing as the way out.”

“You people always ask what it means. It means don’t go down there.”

“You saved him. That does not make this place yours.”

“Tavi knew better. That is what makes me angry.”

Avoid Sela saying:

“The Glasswell is a sacred place of memory.”

Better:

“Some places remember too loudly. Locals call that a warning. Offworlders call it research.”

## Character danger

Do not make her a mystical guide. Her authority comes from lived local knowledge.
